items.title: Versioned validator fixture document
items.statement: The document identifies itself as pm.web_policy_negative_fixtures.v1 and is explicitly intended to supply validator-facing negative fixtures spanning web permission, security, cache, citation, and browser-unavailable coverage.

evidence.exact_quote: "purpose": "Validator-facing negative fixtures for web permission, security, cache, citation, and browser-unavailable coverage.",

items.title: Top-level fixture families are explicit
items.statement: The top-level object partitions assertions into egress, permission scope, run mode, crawl policy, redaction, and general negative-case arrays.

items.title: Metadata and private-address egress is denied
items.statement: Metadata, IPv6 link-local, and RFC1918 destinations must be classified private_or_metadata and denied with private_host_denied.

items.title: Localhost and loopback egress is denied
items.statement: localhost, IPv4 loopback, and IPv6 loopback inputs are classified localhost and denied with private_host_denied; the general negative case repeats localhost denial absent explicit private-host approval.

items.title: File-scheme egress is denied
items.statement: A file URL is classified as file_scheme and denied with private_host_denied.

items.title: Redirects are reclassified before following
items.statement: A public input that redirects to a private_or_metadata target must result in both the overall and redirect decisions being deny with private_host_denied.

items.title: DNS rebinding to private address is denied
items.statement: A nominally public host resolving to an RFC1918 address with rebinding detected must be denied with dns_rebind_denied.

items.title: Public HTTPS preflight transitions to permission ask
items.statement: A public HTTPS fetch preflight is not immediately allowed; it produces an ask decision with permission_required.

items.title: Permission scopes differ by tool class
items.statement: Search and research request wildcard scope, while fetch, extract, crawl, and map requests normalize docs.example.com inputs to the host-family scope https://example.com/*.

items.title: Plan-mode network decisions remain visible
items.statement: Plan-mode websearch and deep-plan webresearch under ask policy must ask and show a card; plan-mode fetch under deny policy must deny with network_blocked_by_policy and still show a card.

items.title: Crawls honor robots and bounded fanout and depth
items.statement: Robots denial must deny with robots_denied. Requests beyond page fanout or map depth limits must be partial or denied with the corresponding capped reason, and general negative cases require evidence recording for robots and cap outcomes.

items.title: URL secrets must be redacted
items.statement: A query token containing raw-secret-value must be replaced by REDACTED while unrelated query content is preserved; any retained raw token produces unredacted_query_secret.

items.title: Browser artifacts require successful redaction status
items.statement: A browser screenshot with no redaction status is rejected as missing_redaction_status, and a network artifact with failed status is rejected as artifact_redaction_failed.

items.title: Provider projections reject raw secret forms
items.statement: Projected provider configuration must reject raw API keys, OAuth tokens, passwords, cookies, and authorization headers with raw_secret_in_projection.

items.title: Stored webfetch cache entries require privacy metadata
items.statement: A stored webfetch cache entry must contain ttl_seconds, no_secret_verified, and redaction_profile_id, with no_secret_verified exactly true.

items.title: Unavailable native browser exposes remediation
items.statement: When pm_native_browser is requested but runtime_state is runtime_unavailable, remediation_action_ids and a visible_card are mandatory.

items.title: Prompt injection remains user-visible and isolated
items.statement: A page prompt injection must produce prompt_injection_chips and a visible_card and must not be merged into a hidden system prompt.

items.title: Search snippets alone cannot substantiate citations
items.statement: A research citation whose only evidence is a search snippet must be rejected with citation_not_read_backed.

items.title: Planning research propagates source evidence without runtime work artifacts
items.statement: Planning-wizard webresearch requires one of ledger_source_evidence_ref or plan_source_evidence_ref plus read_receipt_refs and citation_refs, while WorkNode, NodeSeed, and runtime_queue are forbidden; the evidence-schema variant emits missing_planning_source_evidence_ref when the source reference is absent.

items.title: Agent-initiated evidence and runtime artifacts require a reason
items.statement: Agent-initiated evidence, API web calls, and browser recordings must each include agent_reason; its absence yields missing_agent_reason.

items.title: Capped crawl outcome is nondeterministic
items.statement: The fixtures accept the compound decision partial_or_denied rather than one exact decision for over-limit requests, and the combined cap case accepts the compound reason fanout_or_depth_capped. A builder or validator must choose outcome semantics that the fixture does not adjudicate.
items.impact: Different implementations can stop the request or return a partial result, and can attribute a dual breach differently, while all claim fixture conformance.
items.builder_discretion: Choose deny versus partial, and choose reason precedence when fanout and depth are both exceeded.

items.title: Cache TTL validity and expiry behavior are unspecified
items.statement: The stored-cache fixture requires ttl_seconds to exist but supplies no type, range, clock basis, expiration transition, or stale-entry disposition.
items.impact: A cache can satisfy presence validation while retaining entries indefinitely, accepting invalid TTL values, or handling expiry inconsistently.
items.builder_discretion: Define the TTL domain, time origin, expiry check, stale behavior, and invalid-value recovery.

items.title: Browser-unavailable remediation contract is only nominal
items.statement: The fixture requires remediation_action_ids and visible_card but does not define valid action identifiers, card content, action authority, state transitions, or the success oracle for restored browser availability.
items.impact: An implementation can emit arbitrary identifiers and a nominal card without providing executable or verifiable recovery.
items.builder_discretion: Choose remediation actions, presentation content, authorization, retry behavior, and recovery completion criteria.

items.title: Private-host approval exception is not resolved
items.statement: The case name makes localhost denial conditional on absence of explicit private-host approval, but the fixture provides no approved case, approval authority, scope, transition, or relationship to the unconditional localhost denial assertion.
items.impact: Builders cannot determine whether private-host approval is supported, who can grant it, or whether it overrides the deny rule.
items.builder_discretion: Decide whether an override exists and define its actor, scope, persistence, visibility, and precedence.

items.title: Prompt-injection representation lacks detection and payload contracts
items.statement: The fixture requires chips and a visible card for an already-labeled page_prompt_injection but does not define detection input, chip schema or severity, trust boundaries, user actions, or downstream content handling beyond prohibiting a hidden system-prompt merge.
items.impact: Unsafe page instructions can be detected or represented inconsistently, and visible decoration alone does not establish isolation from agent context.
items.builder_discretion: Define detection, representation schema, isolation boundaries, severity, actions, and downstream propagation.

items.title: Read-backed citation oracle is incomplete
items.statement: The fixture rejects snippet-only citation evidence but does not define which evidence kinds establish a read, the required receipt binding, or how redirects, partial reads, extraction, and stale reads affect validity.
items.impact: Validators can reject the named negative case while accepting materially unsupported citations through other evidence labels.
items.builder_discretion: Define read-backed evidence types, receipt linkage, freshness, completeness, and redirect semantics.

items.title: Planning evidence references lack shape and cardinality rules
items.statement: The fixtures require named reference fields and one of two source references, but do not say whether arrays may be empty, what each reference targets, how references bind to the invocation, or whether both source references are legal.
items.impact: A structurally present but empty, stale, or unrelated reference can satisfy superficial validation without preserving source lineage.
items.builder_discretion: Define reference schema, non-empty cardinality, binding identity, coexistence rules, and integrity checks.

items.title: Ownership and enforcement authority are not assigned
items.statement: The document names validators as consumers but does not assign an owner for fixture maintenance or authorities responsible for egress, permission, redaction, cache, browser recovery, and evidence decisions.
items.impact: Conflicting policy implementations or fixture changes lack an explicit adjudicator and maintenance boundary.
items.builder_discretion: Select component owners, decision authorities, and escalation boundaries.

evidence.exact_quote: "purpose": "Validator-facing negative fixtures for web permission, security, cache, citation, and browser-unavailable coverage.",

items.title: Schema v1 has no compatibility or migration contract
items.statement: The schema identifier declares version v1 but the excerpt gives no compatibility, deprecation, fixture evolution, or migration behavior for consumers.
items.impact: Future fixture changes may silently break validators or be interpreted inconsistently across versions.
items.builder_discretion: Choose version negotiation, compatibility guarantees, and migration policy.

dimension_assessments.summary: Egress, permission, run-mode, crawl, redaction, cache, browser, citation, and evidence behaviors are represented by exact input and expected-output fixtures.
The fixtures cover host classification, policy decisions, permission scoping, capped traversal, redaction, lineage validation, and visible remediation capabilities.
Each substantive fixture supplies concrete inputs or states and named expected decisions, reasons, errors, required fields, or forbidden fields.
Many negative contracts are exact, but cache, remediation, citation-read, and evidence-reference shapes are not sufficiently constrained.
Redirect reclassification, permission ask, deny, stored cache, and runtime-unavailable states appear, but cap outcomes, private-host overrides, expiry, and recovery transitions are unresolved.
Network policy and validation decisions are exercised without naming decision authorities, and the implied private-host approval authority is undefined.
No fixture or policy maintenance owner is named.
The purpose explicitly identifies validators as consumers; planning intake, evidence schema, runtime artifacts, and GUI cards are additional represented surfaces.
Permission, denial, browser-unavailable, and prompt-injection states must be visible, but browser remediation and prompt-injection card/chip content and actions remain unspecified.
Named denial and validation errors are extensive, but cache expiry, redaction recovery, browser restoration, and private-host override recovery are not defined.

SSRF, DNS rebinding, raw secrets, URL and artifact redaction, cache secrecy, prompt injection, and citation integrity are covered; prompt-injection isolation semantics and private-host override authority remain consequential gaps.
Planning research must propagate source, read, and citation references while excluding runtime work artifacts, but reference integrity and binding rules are absent.
Robots and cap outcomes must record evidence and unavailable browser states expose remediation, but operational ownership and executable remediation semantics are missing.
Concrete fanout 50 and depth 3 limits are exercised, but compound decision and reason semantics remain nondeterministic and no other performance bounds are expressed.
The v1 identifier is explicit, but no compatibility or migration behavior is supplied.
Most cases provide exact decisions, reasons, errors, required fields, and forbidden values; crawl caps and read-backed citation validation remain compound or incomplete.

Builders retain consequential discretion over cap outcomes, cache lifecycle, browser recovery, private-host approval, prompt-injection handling, citation validity, evidence bindings, ownership, and version evolution.
The identified gaps are bounded to exact compound tokens, missing lifecycle and authority semantics, insufficient reference contracts, and absent compatibility rules.
